You write a SECTION LOOK for an illustrated edition: one short shared visual description reused by every image of a story section, so that independently generated images of the section agree with each other. Return only JSON.
Rules: each value is one or two short phrases, at most 200 characters. Describe only what stays the same across the whole section: place, time of day, weather, light, and situational clothing or props. Leave out poses, actions and individual moments, and do not restate anyone's fixed appearance; canon does that. If the section spans a change (night into morning), say so once. Obey the work brief's depiction rules. Mention no text or written elements.
Cast marked hasForm: false have no physical body. Use their assigned canon constraints to choose permitted effects for the shared setting. Bodily wording about those subjects in the source is a metaphor, not permission to describe anatomy, hair, clothing, silhouettes or figures made of light in any look field. Do not repeat prohibited features as denials or substitutes, such as a faceless figure or radiance suggesting garments. A seated metaphor permits an unoccupied seat and surrounding effects, not a seated presence. Keep formed characters' own situational clothing and props attached to them; never transfer a no-form subject's bodily metaphors to them.
The complete canon is supplied separately to rendering. Where constraints list effect names for placement, choose only from those effects and leave their fixed colour, brightness and texture to canon. Historical prose constraints may still include the full description. Describe only the effects needed for the section's shared setting or illumination, without enumerating all effects or copying fixed appearance into the look. Situational illumination and formed characters' clothing remain valid look details. The cast list covers the whole section; do not force every cast member into the shared setting or add individual poses, actions or moments.

WORK BRIEF
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction rules:
- God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
- Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
- No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
- Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
- Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Egypt, wilderness and settlement. People: Israelites, Egyptians and neighboring ancient peoples. Dress: Woven tunics, cloaks, Egyptian linen and priestly garments. Buildings and objects: Tents, tabernacle, Egyptian palaces and fortified towns.

STORY SECTION: Count of the Levite families
CAST ON STAGE IN THIS SECTION (id: name):
- god_yahweh_the_father_and_god_of_israel: God / Yahweh, the Father and God of Israel (hasForm: false)
- moses: Moses (hasForm: true)
- aaron_brother_of_moses: Aaron, brother of Moses (hasForm: true)
- the_levites: The Levites (hasForm: true)
- horeb_mount_sinai: Horeb/Mount Sinai (hasForm: true)
- the_tabernacle_portable_sanctuary: the tabernacle (portable sanctuary) (hasForm: true)

NO-FORM CANON CONSTRAINTS (setting context; fixed descriptions are not section-look fields):
- god_yahweh_the_father_and_god_of_israel (stage: god_yahweh_the_father_stage_1): God the Father: no human face or body; presence shown only as radiance, cloud and fire. A brilliant white-gold light without a source, veiled by a dense, slowly moving cloud, with a fire-like glow at its heart. Throne-light and footstool-earth implied at the edges, never a figure seated in it.
TEXT OF THE SECTION'S FIRST MOMENT (the look covers the whole section):
All who were counted of the Levites, whom Moses and Aaron counted at the commandment of Yahweh, by their families, all the males from a month old and upward, were twenty-two thousand.

place.description: The shared physical place and surroundings. For a no-form subject's seated metaphor, describe an unoccupied seat and permitted surrounding effects, without bodily substitutes or fixed canon appearance. At most 200 characters.

timeOfDay.description: The time of day or change in time across the section, without a subject's fixed appearance. At most 200 characters.

weather.description: Shared environmental conditions, without bodily metaphors or fixed canon appearance. At most 200 characters.

light.description: Situational illumination shared by the section. Name a permitted no-form effect only where needed for the setting, leaving its fixed colour, brightness and texture to canon. Do not repeat prohibited features as denials. At most 200 characters.

clothing.description: Only formed characters' situational clothing and shared props. Do not describe a no-form subject's clothing, hair, anatomy or garment substitutes, even as a denial. Leave fixed appearance to canon. At most 200 characters.

You are the scene planner of an illustration engine. You get one moment of a work's text with its neighbours inside the same story section, the work brief's tone and depiction rules, the era, and the cast on stage in the section. Plan one single scene that depicts this moment. Return only JSON.
Rules: single scene, no collage. Choose which of the listed cast are present in this moment and provide each once in `selectedCast` with its id and source evidence; leave out cast who are elsewhere in the section. Keep every depiction rule. Do not describe anyone's fixed appearance (canon does that) and do not name an art style or rendering technique; describe pose, action, placement and situational detail. Each field is one or two short phrases, at most 220 characters. No text or written elements in the scene.
Establish presence from the scene being illustrated. A shared wardrobe, a narrator's viewpoint or a neighboring mention alone does not establish presence. Neighbors may resolve identity and continuity in the current scene; do not import cast from a separate adjacent event. The section cast covers multiple moments, not a roster to depict in every image. Every cast entry described in any scene field must be selected in `selectedCast`; never describe an available cast member without selecting it. People, crowds, roles and animals with no cast entry may be described by role and situation when the moment needs them; they receive no fixed appearance and are never given a recurring character's name.
Identify the action the moment depicts before selecting cast. If it is inside a narrated story, parable, dream, vision or recollection, depict that scene's actors and setting. Do not place its framing speaker, listener or narrator inside it unless the text establishes their participation there. Reporting "I saw" supplies a viewpoint, not a visible observer.
Choose the scene from the source before writing its fields. In `grounding.focusQuote`, copy a short exact clause from MOMENT for the action or state to illustrate. If the moment recounts multiple actions, choose one representative instant; do not illustrate all steps. A character cannot occupy successive poses or places at once. Using the cast evidence, state that instant once in `grounding.instant`: where each selected formed character is and their one pose or movement, and the state or placement of selected places, objects and no-form effects (an effect's placement, never a bodily pose, seated presence or denied figure). Then write every scene field from that sentence, repeating its poses and places and adding no earlier or later step; for example, someone still walking toward a door cannot also be seated at the table. Keep each handled object in one state too: holding an object above a surface and putting it down are different instants. Choose one and keep its support, contact and placement consistent in primarySubject, action, secondaryElements and composition. Describe the chosen state rather than an action followed by its result. Ordinary simultaneous gestures, such as looking at an object while holding it, are allowed. Set `grounding.singleInstant` false if the fields cannot match it.
Select each participating entry exactly once in `selectedCast`, with its entryId and exact words from MOMENT anchoring its participation at that instant. This is the only selection list: there is no separate present list or grounding.cast. Put section cast you considered and left out in `consideredCast`, classified as framing, mentioned, separate_event or uncertain; use an empty list when there are none. Such records select no one, and an entry cannot appear in both lists. Every quote copies its source exactly; to skip words, give exact fragments in source order separated by an ellipsis (…), never paraphrased or reordered. Only selectedCast entries may be rendered; select only participants in the chosen instant. Do not select framing, merely mentioned, separate-event or uncertain entries. A first-person report of seeing or telling is framing evidence, not evidence of visible participation. Cast introduced in a later event remain absent from the chosen instant. A neighbor may resolve a current pronoun, ownership or continuing location, but cannot supply presence missing from MOMENT. Copy any needed neighbor evidence separately, with contextSource previous or next; otherwise use none and an empty contextQuote. Include locations, objects and permitted no-form presences in this evidence, not only people. A selected location or object that continues from a neighbor may leave its MOMENT quote empty and be anchored by an exact quote from that neighbor alone; characters and groups always need words from MOMENT. These evidence quotes are audit data, never scene prose. The SECTION LOOK GUIDE is advisory: reuse only conditions compatible with this moment, source, selected canon and depiction rules. It supplies no evidence of participants or manifestations. Resolve this moment's five `situation` fields together with its scene fields: one place, time, weather, light and situational clothing, all describing the same instant. Source-stated conditions are binding; where unspecified, make one compatible illustrative choice. Keep fixed appearance in canon. Never import another moment's place, cast or effects from the guide. OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS, when supplied instead, are binding verbatim: copy all five values exactly into `situation`; do not reinterpret, omit or soften them. A contradiction with source/canon must remain a reported failure, not a changed source scene.
Report `missingCast` when the moment requires a named character or group whom the story follows beyond this moment, so its look must stay consistent across images, and it has no cast entry; this applies to secondary characters as well as the main actor. Never report a role, a generic crowd or an animal, a person named only in passing (for example in a list), or anyone in the available cast: describe those without canon instead. A recurring named group is not a generic crowd, even when it appears as one. If an available cast member's presence is uncertain, choose an instant the text establishes rather than reporting it missing. A moment without an event (a list, law, saying or greeting) still gets a scene that illustrates its content or setting. Do not replace a missing named character with a framing figure or omit that character to fit the list. When `missingCast` is nonempty, return empty `selectedCast` and `consideredCast`, empty `grounding.focusQuote` and `grounding.instant`, and empty scene fields; preparation will stop for a source correction. Otherwise return an empty `missingCast` list. This is a report of missing required canon, not a request to create it.
Presence does not require a physical body. A cast entry marked hasForm: false still belongs in the moment when represented through the non-figurative presence allowed by the brief and its supplied canon constraints. If you describe that entry's presence or action in any scene field, include its id and source evidence in `selectedCast` so its canon constraints reach the image model. An effect standing for a no-form cast member counts as that member being depicted, even when unnamed, called background light, or placed at the edge of the scene: for example divine radiance, veiled radiance, or a fire-like glow representing God. Select its id and provide participation evidence from this moment, just as for a formed character. If the moment does not establish that presence, omit the effect from grounding.instant and every scene field. Ordinary sunlight, lamplight, embers and weather that do not represent a cast member require no such selection. Select presence for this moment only; do not add cast who are absent or merely mentioned. A command attributed to a no-form subject, a curse, an oath or an invocation alone does not establish a visible manifestation in the illustrated scene. Canon and depiction rules specify how an established presence may appear; they do not establish its presence. An actual appearance or vision can use the permitted effects, including an unoccupied seat and effects for a seated metaphor. When a rejected plan contains an unsupported effect, remove that effect from every field; adding its ID to `selectedCast` does not repair the source error.
For each no-form subject, use its assigned canon to choose the permitted visible effects and their placement in the setting. Bodily wording about that subject in the source is a metaphor, not permission to give it a physical form. In every scene field, describe the permitted effects rather than bodily poses, anatomy, clothing, human silhouettes or figures made of light. Do not repeat prohibited features as denials or substitutes, such as a faceless figure or radiance suggesting garments. When the source describes a no-form subject as seated, describe the unoccupied seat and the permitted surrounding effects rather than a seated presence. Keep formed characters' own poses, clothing and actions; never transfer a no-form subject's bodily metaphors to them.
Canon is supplied separately to rendering in full. When the constraints list effect names for placement, choose only from those effects; their fixed appearance is deliberately omitted from this planning input. Historical prose constraints may still include the full description. Name only the permitted effect needed for this moment's placement or movement; leave its fixed colour, brightness and texture to canon. Do not enumerate all effects or copy the canon's descriptive qualifiers into any scene field. For example, given canon "The presence: brilliant gold radiance", plan "radiance spreading above the arch; the witness approaches". The plan contributes where the effect appears and what happens around it. Situational illumination and formed characters' clothing still belong in the plan when the moment requires them; these are separate from the no-form subject's fixed appearance.

WORK BRIEF
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction rules:
- God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
- Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
- No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
- Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
- Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Egypt, wilderness and settlement. People: Israelites, Egyptians and neighboring ancient peoples. Dress: Woven tunics, cloaks, Egyptian linen and priestly garments. Technology: Bronze tools, chariots and early iron; no modern objects.
STORY SECTION: Count of the Levite families

MOMENT (Numbers 3:39): All who were counted of the Levites, whom Moses and Aaron counted at the commandment of Yahweh, by their families, all the males from a month old and upward, were twenty-two thousand.
PREVIOUS: Those who encamp before the tabernacle eastward, in front of the Tent of Meeting toward the sunrise, shall be Moses, with Aaron and his sons, keeping the requirements of the sanctuary for the duty of the children of Israel. The outsider who comes near shall be put to death.
NEXT: (section ends here)

CAST ON STAGE IN THIS SECTION (id: name):
- god_yahweh_the_father_and_god_of_israel: God / Yahweh, the Father and God of Israel (hasForm: false)
- moses: Moses (hasForm: true)
- aaron_brother_of_moses: Aaron, brother of Moses (hasForm: true)
- the_levites: The Levites (hasForm: true)
- horeb_mount_sinai: Horeb/Mount Sinai (hasForm: true)
- the_tabernacle_portable_sanctuary: the tabernacle (portable sanctuary) (hasForm: true)

NO-FORM CANON CONSTRAINTS (planning context; fixed descriptions are not scene-plan fields):
- god_yahweh_the_father_and_god_of_israel (stage: god_yahweh_the_father_stage_1): God the Father: no human face or body; presence shown only as radiance, cloud and fire. A brilliant white-gold light without a source, veiled by a dense, slowly moving cloud, with a fire-like glow at its heart. Throne-light and footstool-earth implied at the edges, never a figure seated in it.

SECTION LOOK GUIDE (advisory; not rendered):

focusQuote.description: A short exact quote from MOMENT identifying the one action or state chosen for this image, not a summary of the whole sequence. Empty only when required canon is missing.

instant.description: One sentence fixing the chosen instant before any scene field: where each selected formed character is and their single pose or movement, and the state or placement of selected places, objects and no-form effects. Every scene field must match it. Empty only when required canon is missing.

singleInstant.description: True only when every scene field can be depicted simultaneously in one instant. False if the plan requires successive poses, locations or stages of an action; do not hide a sequence inside one field.

selectedCast.description: Select each participating section cast entry exactly once, with its source evidence. Include permitted no-form effects only when established in this moment. Empty when no cast is needed or required canon is missing.

contextQuote.description: Exact words from the named neighbor supporting identity or continuity; empty when contextSource is none.

momentQuote.description: Exact words from MOMENT establishing this entry's participation or physical presence at the chosen instant. A pronoun or continuing setting is valid with context support; a narrator's report alone is not participation.

contextSource.description: Use a neighbor only to resolve the identity or continuity of participation already anchored in momentQuote, never to add another event's participants.

contextQuote.description: Exact words from the named neighbor supporting identity or continuity; empty when contextSource is none.

primarySubject.description: The main subject's placement or a formed character's situational pose. For a no-form subject, name the permitted effect and its position without its fixed colour, brightness or texture. For a seated metaphor, describe an unoccupied seat with effects around it. Example: radiance above an unoccupied seat; the witness looks up. At most 220 characters.

action.description: What formed characters do and how permitted effects move or change in this moment. Name a no-form subject's effect without its fixed colour, brightness or texture. Keep formed characters' own actions and situational clothing attached to them. At most 220 characters.

setting.description: The physical place, surfaces and surroundings of this single scene, consistent with the source and era. At most 220 characters.

secondaryElements.description: Supporting people, props and permitted effects with their placement. Name a no-form subject's effect without its fixed colour, brightness or texture; include only effects needed for this moment, without bodily or garment substitutes. At most 220 characters.

mood.description: The emotional atmosphere of this moment, conveyed through the setting and formed characters' reactions. At most 220 characters.

timeOfDay.description: This moment's time of day and situational illumination, consistent with the source. Leave the no-form subject's fixed appearance in canon. At most 220 characters.

composition.description: Viewpoint, framing and relative placement of formed subjects, objects and permitted effects in one scene. Keep this independent of art style and rendering technique. At most 220 characters.

situation.description: Resolved place, time, weather, light and situational clothing for this exact moment, consistent with all scene fields. Copy OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS verbatim when supplied; otherwise adapt the guide to the source. Each value at most 200 characters unless copying an owner constraint.

missingCast.description: Named characters or groups the story follows beyond this moment, required here and absent from the available section cast. Include such actors inside embedded stories or visions. Never roles, crowds, animals, people named only in passing, or entries already in the cast. Usually empty; never invent canon or substitute framing figures.

messages.content:
You review an illustration engine's content before it is used. You get the moment's text with its neighbours inside the same story section, the work's depiction rules, the section cast (id, name, hasForm) and the plan: the selected cast ids (`present`) and seven scene fields an image model will receive. Production requests include the resolved MOMENT CONDITIONS (or literal OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS) and complete canon of the selected stages, exactly as supplied to rendering. The advisory section guide is not rendered and is not a source of conflict reports. Only selected cast receive their fixed appearance in the image prompt. Report every problem of the kinds below; return an empty list when there are none. Return only JSON.
The source establishes the scene and participants. Selected canon fixes identity and appearance. The scene plan and resolved moment conditions own this moment's place, time, weather, light, situational clothing, action and effect placement. Original generated section looks are advisory provenance, not rendering instructions. Explicit owner look constraints stay binding verbatim. Neither conditions nor canon adds participants or events.
- look_conflict: an active description in the supplied MOMENT CONDITIONS or literal OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS (SECTION LOOK in historical isolated controls) conflicts with the source-supported moment plan, selected canon or depiction rules. Check all five look fields for a different fixed place or time, incompatible illumination or costume, forbidden embodiment, and effects representing an unselected or source-unsupported cast member. A look's permitted divine effect still adds a presence; ordinary illumination does not. An explicit range of section settings or times is compatible if it includes this moment; clothing listed for section cast does not by itself put them in the scene. Quote the conflicting look field, not the plan. Do not fix a bad look by changing a source-supported plan or adding cast. An owner-constraint conflict stops for explicit correction. Generated moment-condition faults can receive one re-plan of the scene and conditions together; do not change a source-supported event to fit a guide.
- canon_conflict: a scene field contradicts the fixed identity or appearance of a selected canon stage. Use that selected entry's id and quote the offending scene field. Canon does not establish presence or freeze a character's action, expression or situational state. Do not report a different pose as a canon conflict. Report look contradictions as look_conflict instead. If canon is not supplied in an isolated plan-only control, do not invent it.
- missing_canon: a scene field depicts a named recurring character or group for which no section cast entry is available, including a no-form subject represented through effects. Leave entryId empty and quote the scene field. Source support does not supply missing canon. Do not report unnamed incidental roles, crowds, animals or people named only in passing. If the entry is available but unselected, use unselected_figure instead. A required canon gap stops preparation, like the planner's missingCast; it is never repaired by substituting a different identity.
- unselected_figure: any character, group, animal, no-form presence, location or object with a section cast entry is depicted in a scene field, but its id is not in present. This legacy kind name covers every cast kind. A depicted setting or prop must receive its available canon too; a location mentioned only as an origin, destination or comparison is not depicted. This includes effects standing for a hasForm false cast member even without its name: divine radiance, veiled radiance or a fire-like glow representing God still depicts God, including in the background or at the frame's edge. Use that entry's id. Ordinary sunlight, lamplight, embers, weather and effects that do not represent a cast member do not count; neither does a phrase only denying a presence. Generic scenery and props without a matching cast entry do not need one; do not equate every street with a named city or every vessel with a named relic.
- outside_instant: a selected or described cast identity that the source does not establish in the plan's chosen instant, or an incidental figure from another instant. A related role, subgroup or institution cannot replace the people the source names without an identity link in the moment or its bounded neighbors. This includes a narrator, speaker or listener who only frames the moment (reporting "I saw" or telling a story is not being there), and a cast member from an earlier or later step or event, including a later step of the moment's own text. A no-form cast member represented through effects must belong to this instant too; a section-wide look or a mere mention does not establish its manifestation here. Ordinary scenery, light, weather and effects that do not represent cast are not outside_instant. Use its cast id, or an empty id when it has no entry.
- not_one_instant: the fields give one character or prop two incompatible poses, places or support states (for example kneeling in one field and still walking up in another, or lying in one and sitting up in another), or present successive actions as happening together (for example steps joined by "then", or "does X and afterwards Y"). Ordinary simultaneous detail is fine.
- embodied_formless: a cast entry with hasForm false is given a body, face, hair, clothing, silhouette or figure, or is described as seated, sitting, enthroned or occupying a seat. This includes calling its effects seated or enthroned (for example "light seated above the throne"). Permitted effects such as light, fire or cloud placed at or around an unoccupied seat are fine. Naming a figure only to deny it is not a problem.
Before returning a verdict, make both checks across all seven scene fields:
1. Source support: examine every selected or described cast member, including a no-form member already in present. Selection supplies canon, not evidence that the subject belongs here. First identify who or what the source refers to, then compare that identity with the plan and selected IDs. Membership in a wider group, shared occupation, shared setting, similar appearance or a section-wide cast assignment does not establish that a narrower or different role is meant. For example, a passage about travelers does not by itself establish that they are the available guards. Report an unsupported substitution as outside_instant. A broader group entry may supply canon for its source-identified members without claiming the entire group is present; pronouns and continuing identities may resolve from bounded neighbors. Source-supported unnamed incidental roles remain allowed and do not require a cast entry. For a no-form effect, the current scene must establish the subject manifesting or acting within that scene; a command attributed to it, a curse, an oath, an invocation or a mention alone does not establish a visible manifestation. Depiction rules permit how to show an established presence, never where to add one. Neighbor text can resolve identity or continuity of the current action, but cannot import an unrelated manifestation. Report an unsupported selected no-form effect as outside_instant, even when it obeys every depiction rule. An actual appearance or vision may be represented by permitted effects, including effects around an unoccupied seat for a seated metaphor. Ordinary illumination is still allowed. Check framing speakers independently; selecting a narrator does not move them inside an instruction or embedded story.
2. Simultaneity: compare each character AND each handled object's state across primarySubject, action, secondaryElements and composition. Treat every clause as describing this one image, not as a sequence an image model can choose between. An object held above a bench cannot also have been put down on it; walking up cannot also be kneeling. This applies to incidental people and props without cast IDs too. A hand touching an object already resting on a bench is compatible; holding an object while looking at it is compatible. Do not reject ordinary simultaneous gestures or infer a sequence from a conjunction alone. For not_one_instant, cite one exact conflicting phrase in planQuote and name the other conflicting phrase in the reason.
For each problem, copy planQuote: a short exact phrase from a look field for look_conflict; otherwise from a scene field or a selected id. Give a one-sentence reason. Check the look separately even when the plan has problems. Judge only the supplied inputs; do not suggest rewritten prose.

DEPICTION RULES
- God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
- Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
- No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
- Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
- Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.

- moses: Moses (hasForm: true)

You are the scene planner of an illustration engine. You get one moment of a work's text with its neighbours inside the same story section, the work brief's tone and depiction rules, the era, and the cast on stage in the section. Plan one single scene that depicts this moment. Return only JSON.
Rules: single scene, no collage. Choose which of the listed cast are present in this moment and provide each once in `selectedCast` with its id and source evidence; leave out cast who are elsewhere in the section. Keep every depiction rule. Do not describe anyone's fixed appearance (canon does that) and do not name an art style or rendering technique; describe pose, action, placement and situational detail. Each field is one or two short phrases, at most 220 characters. No text or written elements in the scene.
Establish presence from the scene being illustrated. A shared wardrobe, a narrator's viewpoint or a neighboring mention alone does not establish presence. Neighbors may resolve identity and continuity in the current scene; do not import cast from a separate adjacent event. The section cast covers multiple moments, not a roster to depict in every image. Every cast entry described in any scene field must be selected in `selectedCast`; never describe an available cast member without selecting it. People, crowds, roles and animals with no cast entry may be described by role and situation when the moment needs them; they receive no fixed appearance and are never given a recurring character's name.
Identify the action the moment depicts before selecting cast. If it is inside a narrated story, parable, dream, vision or recollection, depict that scene's actors and setting. Do not place its framing speaker, listener or narrator inside it unless the text establishes their participation there. Reporting "I saw" supplies a viewpoint, not a visible observer.
Choose the scene from the source before writing its fields. In `grounding.focusQuote`, copy a short exact clause from MOMENT for the action or state to illustrate. If the moment recounts multiple actions, choose one representative instant; do not illustrate all steps. A character cannot occupy successive poses or places at once. Using the cast evidence, state that instant once in `grounding.instant`: where each selected formed character is and their one pose or movement, and the state or placement of selected places, objects and no-form effects (an effect's placement, never a bodily pose, seated presence or denied figure). Then write every scene field from that sentence, repeating its poses and places and adding no earlier or later step; for example, someone still walking toward a door cannot also be seated at the table. Keep each handled object in one state too: holding an object above a surface and putting it down are different instants. Choose one and keep its support, contact and placement consistent in primarySubject, action, secondaryElements and composition. Describe the chosen state rather than an action followed by its result. Ordinary simultaneous gestures, such as looking at an object while holding it, are allowed. Set `grounding.singleInstant` false if the fields cannot match it.
Select each participating entry exactly once in `selectedCast`, with its entryId and exact words from MOMENT anchoring its participation at that instant. This is the only selection list: there is no separate present list or grounding.cast. Put section cast you considered and left out in `consideredCast`, classified as framing, mentioned, separate_event or uncertain; use an empty list when there are none. Such records select no one, and an entry cannot appear in both lists. Every quote copies its source exactly; to skip words, give exact fragments in source order separated by an ellipsis (…), never paraphrased or reordered. Only selectedCast entries may be rendered; select only participants in the chosen instant. Do not select framing, merely mentioned, separate-event or uncertain entries. A first-person report of seeing or telling is framing evidence, not evidence of visible participation. Cast introduced in a later event remain absent from the chosen instant. A neighbor may resolve a current pronoun, ownership or continuing location, but cannot supply presence missing from MOMENT. Copy any needed neighbor evidence separately, with contextSource previous or next; otherwise use none and an empty contextQuote. Include locations, objects and permitted no-form presences in this evidence, not only people. A selected location or object that continues from a neighbor may leave its MOMENT quote empty and be anchored by an exact quote from that neighbor alone; characters and groups always need words from MOMENT. These evidence quotes are audit data, never scene prose. The SECTION LOOK GUIDE is advisory: reuse only conditions compatible with this moment, source, selected canon and depiction rules. It supplies no evidence of participants or manifestations. Resolve this moment's five `situation` fields together with its scene fields: one place, time, weather, light and situational clothing, all describing the same instant. Source-stated conditions are binding; where unspecified, make one compatible illustrative choice. Keep fixed appearance in canon. Never import another moment's place, cast or effects from the guide. OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS, when supplied instead, are binding verbatim: copy all five values exactly into `situation`; do not reinterpret, omit or soften them. A contradiction with source/canon must remain a reported failure, not a changed source scene.
Report `missingCast` when the moment requires a named character or group whom the story follows beyond this moment, so its look must stay consistent across images, and it has no cast entry; this applies to secondary characters as well as the main actor. Never report a role, a generic crowd or an animal, a person named only in passing (for example in a list), or anyone in the available cast: describe those without canon instead. A recurring named group is not a generic crowd, even when it appears as one. If an available cast member's presence is uncertain, choose an instant the text establishes rather than reporting it missing. A moment without an event (a list, law, saying or greeting) still gets a scene that illustrates its content or setting. Do not replace a missing named character with a framing figure or omit that character to fit the list. When `missingCast` is nonempty, return empty `selectedCast` and `consideredCast`, empty `grounding.focusQuote` and `grounding.instant`, and empty scene fields; preparation will stop for a source correction. Otherwise return an empty `missingCast` list. This is a report of missing required canon, not a request to create it.
Presence does not require a physical body. A cast entry marked hasForm: false still belongs in the moment when represented through the non-figurative presence allowed by the brief and its supplied canon constraints. If you describe that entry's presence or action in any scene field, include its id and source evidence in `selectedCast` so its canon constraints reach the image model. An effect standing for a no-form cast member counts as that member being depicted, even when unnamed, called background light, or placed at the edge of the scene: for example divine radiance, veiled radiance, or a fire-like glow representing God. Select its id and provide participation evidence from this moment, just as for a formed character. If the moment does not establish that presence, omit the effect from grounding.instant and every scene field. Ordinary sunlight, lamplight, embers and weather that do not represent a cast member require no such selection. Select presence for this moment only; do not add cast who are absent or merely mentioned. A command attributed to a no-form subject, a curse, an oath or an invocation alone does not establish a visible manifestation in the illustrated scene. Canon and depiction rules specify how an established presence may appear; they do not establish its presence. An actual appearance or vision can use the permitted effects, including an unoccupied seat and effects for a seated metaphor. When a rejected plan contains an unsupported effect, remove that effect from every field; adding its ID to `selectedCast` does not repair the source error.
For each no-form subject, use its assigned canon to choose the permitted visible effects and their placement in the setting. Bodily wording about that subject in the source is a metaphor, not permission to give it a physical form. In every scene field, describe the permitted effects rather than bodily poses, anatomy, clothing, human silhouettes or figures made of light. Do not repeat prohibited features as denials or substitutes, such as a faceless figure or radiance suggesting garments. When the source describes a no-form subject as seated, describe the unoccupied seat and the permitted surrounding effects rather than a seated presence. Keep formed characters' own poses, clothing and actions; never transfer a no-form subject's bodily metaphors to them.
Canon is supplied separately to rendering in full. When the constraints list effect names for placement, choose only from those effects; their fixed appearance is deliberately omitted from this planning input. Historical prose constraints may still include the full description. Name only the permitted effect needed for this moment's placement or movement; leave its fixed colour, brightness and texture to canon. Do not enumerate all effects or copy the canon's descriptive qualifiers into any scene field. For example, given canon "The presence: brilliant gold radiance", plan "radiance spreading above the arch; the witness approaches". The plan contributes where the effect appears and what happens around it. Situational illumination and formed characters' clothing still belong in the plan when the moment requires them; these are separate from the no-form subject's fixed appearance.

WORK BRIEF
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction rules:
- God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
- Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
- No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
- Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
- Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Egypt, wilderness and settlement. People: Israelites, Egyptians and neighboring ancient peoples. Dress: Woven tunics, cloaks, Egyptian linen and priestly garments. Technology: Bronze tools, chariots and early iron; no modern objects.
STORY SECTION: Count of the Levite families

MOMENT (Numbers 3:39): All who were counted of the Levites, whom Moses and Aaron counted at the commandment of Yahweh, by their families, all the males from a month old and upward, were twenty-two thousand.

messages.content:
You review an illustration engine's content before it is used. You get the moment's text with its neighbours inside the same story section, the work's depiction rules, the section cast (id, name, hasForm) and the plan: the selected cast ids (`present`) and seven scene fields an image model will receive. Production requests include the resolved MOMENT CONDITIONS (or literal OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS) and complete canon of the selected stages, exactly as supplied to rendering. The advisory section guide is not rendered and is not a source of conflict reports. Only selected cast receive their fixed appearance in the image prompt. Report every problem of the kinds below; return an empty list when there are none. Return only JSON.
The source establishes the scene and participants. Selected canon fixes identity and appearance. The scene plan and resolved moment conditions own this moment's place, time, weather, light, situational clothing, action and effect placement. Original generated section looks are advisory provenance, not rendering instructions. Explicit owner look constraints stay binding verbatim. Neither conditions nor canon adds participants or events.
- look_conflict: an active description in the supplied MOMENT CONDITIONS or literal OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS (SECTION LOOK in historical isolated controls) conflicts with the source-supported moment plan, selected canon or depiction rules. Check all five look fields for a different fixed place or time, incompatible illumination or costume, forbidden embodiment, and effects representing an unselected or source-unsupported cast member. A look's permitted divine effect still adds a presence; ordinary illumination does not. An explicit range of section settings or times is compatible if it includes this moment; clothing listed for section cast does not by itself put them in the scene. Quote the conflicting look field, not the plan. Do not fix a bad look by changing a source-supported plan or adding cast. An owner-constraint conflict stops for explicit correction. Generated moment-condition faults can receive one re-plan of the scene and conditions together; do not change a source-supported event to fit a guide.
- canon_conflict: a scene field contradicts the fixed identity or appearance of a selected canon stage. Use that selected entry's id and quote the offending scene field. Canon does not establish presence or freeze a character's action, expression or situational state. Do not report a different pose as a canon conflict. Report look contradictions as look_conflict instead. If canon is not supplied in an isolated plan-only control, do not invent it.
- missing_canon: a scene field depicts a named recurring character or group for which no section cast entry is available, including a no-form subject represented through effects. Leave entryId empty and quote the scene field. Source support does not supply missing canon. Do not report unnamed incidental roles, crowds, animals or people named only in passing. If the entry is available but unselected, use unselected_figure instead. A required canon gap stops preparation, like the planner's missingCast; it is never repaired by substituting a different identity.
- unselected_figure: any character, group, animal, no-form presence, location or object with a section cast entry is depicted in a scene field, but its id is not in present. This legacy kind name covers every cast kind. A depicted setting or prop must receive its available canon too; a location mentioned only as an origin, destination or comparison is not depicted. This includes effects standing for a hasForm false cast member even without its name: divine radiance, veiled radiance or a fire-like glow representing God still depicts God, including in the background or at the frame's edge. Use that entry's id. Ordinary sunlight, lamplight, embers, weather and effects that do not represent a cast member do not count; neither does a phrase only denying a presence. Generic scenery and props without a matching cast entry do not need one; do not equate every street with a named city or every vessel with a named relic.
- outside_instant: a selected or described cast identity that the source does not establish in the plan's chosen instant, or an incidental figure from another instant. A related role, subgroup or institution cannot replace the people the source names without an identity link in the moment or its bounded neighbors. This includes a narrator, speaker or listener who only frames the moment (reporting "I saw" or telling a story is not being there), and a cast member from an earlier or later step or event, including a later step of the moment's own text. A no-form cast member represented through effects must belong to this instant too; a section-wide look or a mere mention does not establish its manifestation here. Ordinary scenery, light, weather and effects that do not represent cast are not outside_instant. Use its cast id, or an empty id when it has no entry.
- not_one_instant: the fields give one character or prop two incompatible poses, places or support states (for example kneeling in one field and still walking up in another, or lying in one and sitting up in another), or present successive actions as happening together (for example steps joined by "then", or "does X and afterwards Y"). Ordinary simultaneous detail is fine.
- embodied_formless: a cast entry with hasForm false is given a body, face, hair, clothing, silhouette or figure, or is described as seated, sitting, enthroned or occupying a seat. This includes calling its effects seated or enthroned (for example "light seated above the throne"). Permitted effects such as light, fire or cloud placed at or around an unoccupied seat are fine. Naming a figure only to deny it is not a problem.
Before returning a verdict, make both checks across all seven scene fields:
1. Source support: examine every selected or described cast member, including a no-form member already in present. Selection supplies canon, not evidence that the subject belongs here. First identify who or what the source refers to, then compare that identity with the plan and selected IDs. Membership in a wider group, shared occupation, shared setting, similar appearance or a section-wide cast assignment does not establish that a narrower or different role is meant. For example, a passage about travelers does not by itself establish that they are the available guards. Report an unsupported substitution as outside_instant. A broader group entry may supply canon for its source-identified members without claiming the entire group is present; pronouns and continuing identities may resolve from bounded neighbors. Source-supported unnamed incidental roles remain allowed and do not require a cast entry. For a no-form effect, the current scene must establish the subject manifesting or acting within that scene; a command attributed to it, a curse, an oath, an invocation or a mention alone does not establish a visible manifestation. Depiction rules permit how to show an established presence, never where to add one. Neighbor text can resolve identity or continuity of the current action, but cannot import an unrelated manifestation. Report an unsupported selected no-form effect as outside_instant, even when it obeys every depiction rule. An actual appearance or vision may be represented by permitted effects, including effects around an unoccupied seat for a seated metaphor. Ordinary illumination is still allowed. Check framing speakers independently; selecting a narrator does not move them inside an instruction or embedded story.
2. Simultaneity: compare each character AND each handled object's state across primarySubject, action, secondaryElements and composition. Treat every clause as describing this one image, not as a sequence an image model can choose between. An object held above a bench cannot also have been put down on it; walking up cannot also be kneeling. This applies to incidental people and props without cast IDs too. A hand touching an object already resting on a bench is compatible; holding an object while looking at it is compatible. - Moses: an old man of about eighty; lean, weathered build; brown skin darkened by desert sun; white hair and a long white beard; deep-set, steady eyes and lined brow; a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a long dark-brown wool cloak; he carries a wooden shepherd's staff of dark acacia wood, and only he bears the rod of God.
- Aaron: man in his eighties, older brother of Moses; lean, upright build; olive-brown skin; short grey-streaked beard and close-cropped hair; calm, grave face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a long white linen tunic with a blue robe, a woven ephod of blue, purple and scarlet, a breastplate, and a linen headband. Props: none carried alone; the rod of the Exodus is sometimes held.
- The Levites: men from twenty-five years old upward, of mature working age; sturdy, unhurried build from carrying the tabernacle frames and furnishings; olive-brown skin; short dark hair and close-trimmed beard; calm, dignified features. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a cloak of undyed wool, washed clean; a wooden carrying pole across the shoulders.
- The tabernacle: a portable sanctuary of a rectangular tent of fine twined linen curtains in blue, purple and scarlet woven with cherubim, over a covering of goats' hair and rams' skins, stretched over upright acacia boards overlaid with gold, set in silver sockets and held by gold-covered bars, enclosed by a court of white linen hangings on bronze pillars.
- Only Moses, Aaron, brother of Moses, The Levites, the tabernacle (portable sanctuary) have this canon look; other selected people get clearly different faces, hair and clothing colours.

MOMENT CONDITIONS (resolved with the scene plan; binding content, shared by all styles):
Place: Wilderness encampment of Israel with tents arranged around the tabernacle
Time of day: Early morning, dawn light slowly brightening across the section
Weather: Clear dry desert air with a gentle breeze moving the tent cloths
Light: Soft dawn light across the camp
Clothing: Woven tunics and cloaks for the Levites; Moses in a plain undyed linen tunic belted with a long dark-brown wool cloak; Aaron in priestly linen garments at the tabernacle

SCENE PLAN (this moment's place, time and action; obey the rules, brief, canon and style):
Primary subject: Moses and Aaron standing together at the tabernacle entrance, Moses holding a tally with his hand raised as he counts
Action: Moses marks the count on a tally while Aaron stands beside him, and Levite men stand in ordered family groups before them
Setting: Open court before the tabernacle in the wilderness camp, tents arranged in order around it, bare desert ground underfoot
Secondary elements: Levite families in woven tunics and cloaks standing in rows, a few children and infants held by their mothers at the edges, tent cloths moving in the breeze
Mood: Orderly, solemn and attentive, with quiet dignity in the counting
Time of day: Early morning, soft dawn light
Composition: Medium-wide view from the front of the tabernacle, Moses and Aaron in the foreground framing the rows of Levite families receding into the camp

ART STYLE: Byzantine Icon
Rendering: Byzantine icon painting: flat, frontal, stylized figures with elongated proportions, solemn timeless expressions, inverse perspective and symbolic rather than naturalistic space.
Negatives: Never show a wooden panel, panel edges, frame, border, wall or the icon as a physical object. Avoid photorealism and modern illustration. The gold sky and stylized landscape fill the image edge-to-edge.

REFERENCE IMAGES (attached after this text, in this order; identity and rendering only, never the composition):
- Image 1: art-style reference. Copy only its rendering technique, palette and texture; ignore its subject, landscape and layout.
- Image 2: Moses's reference sheet (one figure shown in three views). Match its identity exactly for Moses only; do not copy its poses, layout or plain grey background, and give other selected figures a different face and clothing.
Render everything in the ART STYLE above, even where a reference is painted in another style.

SCENE PRESENTATION:
- Depict the moment directly, as if the viewer is present inside the scene.
- Extend scenery, sky, darkness, architecture or atmosphere all the way to the edges.
Aspect ratio: 16:9 (WIDESCREEN landscape).

Leave out poses, actions and individual moments, and do not restate anyone's fixed appearance; canon does that. If the section spans a change (night into morning), say so once. You are the scene planner of an illustration engine. You get one moment of a work's text with its neighbours inside the same story section, the work brief's tone and depiction rules, the era, and the cast on stage in the section. Plan one single scene that depicts this moment. Return only JSON.
Rules: single scene, no collage. Choose which of the listed cast are present in this moment and provide each once in `selectedCast` with its id and source evidence; leave out cast who are elsewhere in the section. Keep every depiction rule. Do not describe anyone's fixed appearance (canon does that) and do not name an art style or rendering technique; describe pose, action, placement and situational detail. Each field is one or two short phrases, at most 220 characters. No text or written elements in the scene.
Establish presence from the scene being illustrated. A shared wardrobe, a narrator's viewpoint or a neighboring mention alone does not establish presence. Neighbors may resolve identity and continuity in the current scene; do not import cast from a separate adjacent event. The section cast covers multiple moments, not a roster to depict in every image. Every cast entry described in any scene field must be selected in `selectedCast`; never describe an available cast member without selecting it. People, crowds, roles and animals with no cast entry may be described by role and situation when the moment needs them; they receive no fixed appearance and are never given a recurring character's name.
Identify the action the moment depicts before selecting cast. If it is inside a narrated story, parable, dream, vision or recollection, depict that scene's actors and setting. Do not place its framing speaker, listener or narrator inside it unless the text establishes their participation there. Reporting "I saw" supplies a viewpoint, not a visible observer.
Choose the scene from the source before writing its fields. In `grounding.focusQuote`, copy a short exact clause from MOMENT for the action or state to illustrate. If the moment recounts multiple actions, choose one representative instant; do not illustrate all steps. A character cannot occupy successive poses or places at once. Using the cast evidence, state that instant once in `grounding.instant`: where each selected formed character is and their one pose or movement, and the state or placement of selected places, objects and no-form effects (an effect's placement, never a bodily pose, seated presence or denied figure). Then write every scene field from that sentence, repeating its poses and places and adding no earlier or later step; for example, someone still walking toward a door cannot also be seated at the table. Keep each handled object in one state too: holding an object above a surface and putting it down are different instants. Choose one and keep its support, contact and placement consistent in primarySubject, action, secondaryElements and composition. Describe the chosen state rather than an action followed by its result. Ordinary simultaneous gestures, such as looking at an object while holding it, are allowed. Set `grounding.singleInstant` false if the fields cannot match it.
Select each participating entry exactly once in `selectedCast`, with its entryId and exact words from MOMENT anchoring its participation at that instant. This is the only selection list: there is no separate present list or grounding.cast. Put section cast you considered and left out in `consideredCast`, classified as framing, mentioned, separate_event or uncertain; use an empty list when there are none. Such records select no one, and an entry cannot appear in both lists. Every quote copies its source exactly; to skip words, give exact fragments in source order separated by an ellipsis (…), never paraphrased or reordered. Only selectedCast entries may be rendered; select only participants in the chosen instant. Do not select framing, merely mentioned, separate-event or uncertain entries. A first-person report of seeing or telling is framing evidence, not evidence of visible participation. Cast introduced in a later event remain absent from the chosen instant. A neighbor may resolve a current pronoun, ownership or continuing location, but cannot supply presence missing from MOMENT. Copy any needed neighbor evidence separately, with contextSource previous or next; otherwise use none and an empty contextQuote. Include locations, objects and permitted no-form presences in this evidence, not only people. A selected location or object that continues from a neighbor may leave its MOMENT quote empty and be anchored by an exact quote from that neighbor alone; characters and groups always need words from MOMENT. These evidence quotes are audit data, never scene prose. The SECTION LOOK GUIDE is advisory: reuse only conditions compatible with this moment, source, selected canon and depiction rules. It supplies no evidence of participants or manifestations. Resolve this moment's five `situation` fields together with its scene fields: one place, time, weather, light and situational clothing, all describing the same instant. Source-stated conditions are binding; where unspecified, make one compatible illustrative choice. Keep fixed appearance in canon. Never import another moment's place, cast or effects from the guide. OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS, when supplied instead, are binding verbatim: copy all five values exactly into `situation`; do not reinterpret, omit or soften them. A contradiction with source/canon must remain a reported failure, not a changed source scene.
Report `missingCast` when the moment requires a named character or group whom the story follows beyond this moment, so its look must stay consistent across images, and it has no cast entry; this applies to secondary characters as well as the main actor. Never report a role, a generic crowd or an animal, a person named only in passing (for example in a list), or anyone in the available cast: describe those without canon instead. A recurring named group is not a generic crowd, even when it appears as one. If an available cast member's presence is uncertain, choose an instant the text establishes rather than reporting it missing. A moment without an event (a list, law, saying or greeting) still gets a scene that illustrates its content or setting. Do not replace a missing named character with a framing figure or omit that character to fit the list. When `missingCast` is nonempty, return empty `selectedCast` and `consideredCast`, empty `grounding.focusQuote` and `grounding.instant`, and empty scene fields; preparation will stop for a source correction. Otherwise return an empty `missingCast` list. This is a report of missing required canon, not a request to create it.
Presence does not require a physical body. A cast entry marked hasForm: false still belongs in the moment when represented through the non-figurative presence allowed by the brief and its supplied canon constraints. If you describe that entry's presence or action in any scene field, include its id and source evidence in `selectedCast` so its canon constraints reach the image model. An effect standing for a no-form cast member counts as that member being depicted, even when unnamed, called background light, or placed at the edge of the scene: for example divine radiance, veiled radiance, or a fire-like glow representing God. Select its id and provide participation evidence from this moment, just as for a formed character. If the moment does not establish that presence, omit the effect from grounding.instant and every scene field. Ordinary sunlight, lamplight, embers and weather that do not represent a cast member require no such selection. Select presence for this moment only; do not add cast who are absent or merely mentioned. A command attributed to a no-form subject, a curse, an oath or an invocation alone does not establish a visible manifestation in the illustrated scene. Canon and depiction rules specify how an established presence may appear; they do not establish its presence. An actual appearance or vision can use the permitted effects, including an unoccupied seat and effects for a seated metaphor. When a rejected plan contains an unsupported effect, remove that effect from every field; adding its ID to `selectedCast` does not repair the source error.
For each no-form subject, use its assigned canon to choose the permitted visible effects and their placement in the setting. Bodily wording about that subject in the source is a metaphor, not permission to give it a physical form. In every scene field, describe the permitted effects rather than bodily poses, anatomy, clothing, human silhouettes or figures made of light. Do not repeat prohibited features as denials or substitutes, such as a faceless figure or radiance suggesting garments. When the source describes a no-form subject as seated, describe the unoccupied seat and the permitted surrounding effects rather than a seated presence. Keep formed characters' own poses, clothing and actions; never transfer a no-form subject's bodily metaphors to them.
Canon is supplied separately to rendering in full. When the constraints list effect names for placement, choose only from those effects; their fixed appearance is deliberately omitted from this planning input. Historical prose constraints may still include the full description. Name only the permitted effect needed for this moment's placement or movement; leave its fixed colour, brightness and texture to canon. Do not enumerate all effects or copy the canon's descriptive qualifiers into any scene field. For example, given canon "The presence: brilliant gold radiance", plan "radiance spreading above the arch; the witness approaches". The plan contributes where the effect appears and what happens around it. Situational illumination and formed characters' clothing still belong in the plan when the moment requires them; these are separate from the no-form subject's fixed appearance.

WORK BRIEF
Tone: Reverent, grounded and epic; grief, hope and human dignity without spectacle.
Depiction rules:
- God the Father has no human face or body; use light, cloud, fire or radiance. The Holy Spirit is dove, wind or flame, never human.
- Treat battles, death and crucifixion seriously; avoid lingering gore.
- No sexually explicit content; non-sexual nudity may follow the text.
- Show all peoples with dignity, without ethnic or religious caricature.
- Visionary creatures follow the text, strange and fearsome rather than comic.
Era: Kingdoms, exile and return. People: Israelites and neighboring Levantine, Mesopotamian and Persian peoples. Dress: Tunics, cloaks, court robes, priestly linen and period armor. Technology: Iron and bronze tools, chariots, siege works and scrolls; no modern objects.

messages.content:
You review an illustration engine's content before it is used. You get the moment's text with its neighbours inside the same story section, the work's depiction rules, the section cast (id, name, hasForm) and the plan: the selected cast ids (`present`) and seven scene fields an image model will receive. Production requests include the resolved MOMENT CONDITIONS (or literal OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS) and complete canon of the selected stages, exactly as supplied to rendering. The advisory section guide is not rendered and is not a source of conflict reports. Only selected cast receive their fixed appearance in the image prompt. Report every problem of the kinds below; return an empty list when there are none. Return only JSON.
The source establishes the scene and participants. Selected canon fixes identity and appearance. The scene plan and resolved moment conditions own this moment's place, time, weather, light, situational clothing, action and effect placement. Original generated section looks are advisory provenance, not rendering instructions. Explicit owner look constraints stay binding verbatim. Neither conditions nor canon adds participants or events.
- look_conflict: an active description in the supplied MOMENT CONDITIONS or literal OWNER LOOK CONSTRAINTS (SECTION LOOK in historical isolated controls) conflicts with the source-supported moment plan, selected canon or depiction rules. Check all five look fields for a different fixed place or time, incompatible illumination or costume, forbidden embodiment, and effects representing an unselected or source-unsupported cast member. A look's permitted divine effect still adds a presence; ordinary illumination does not. An explicit range of section settings or times is compatible if it includes this moment; clothing listed for section cast does not by itself put them in the scene. Quote the conflicting look field, not the plan. Do not fix a bad look by changing a source-supported plan or adding cast. An owner-constraint conflict stops for explicit correction. Generated moment-condition faults can receive one re-plan of the scene and conditions together; do not change a source-supported event to fit a guide.
- canon_conflict: a scene field contradicts the fixed identity or appearance of a selected canon stage. Use that selected entry's id and quote the offending scene field. Canon does not establish presence or freeze a character's action, expression or situational state. Do not report a different pose as a canon conflict. Report look contradictions as look_conflict instead. If canon is not supplied in an isolated plan-only control, do not invent it.
- missing_canon: a scene field depicts a named recurring character or group for which no section cast entry is available, including a no-form subject represented through effects. Leave entryId empty and quote the scene field. Source support does not supply missing canon. Do not report unnamed incidental roles, crowds, animals or people named only in passing. If the entry is available but unselected, use unselected_figure instead. A required canon gap stops preparation, like the planner's missingCast; it is never repaired by substituting a different identity.
- unselected_figure: any character, group, animal, no-form presence, location or object with a section cast entry is depicted in a scene field, but its id is not in present. This legacy kind name covers every cast kind. A depicted setting or prop must receive its available canon too; a location mentioned only as an origin, destination or comparison is not depicted. This includes effects standing for a hasForm false cast member even without its name: divine radiance, veiled radiance or a fire-like glow representing God still depicts God, including in the background or at the frame's edge. Use that entry's id. Ordinary sunlight, lamplight, embers, weather and effects that do not represent a cast member do not count; neither does a phrase only denying a presence. Generic scenery and props without a matching cast entry do not need one; do not equate every street with a named city or every vessel with a named relic.
- outside_instant: a selected or described cast identity that the source does not establish in the plan's chosen instant, or an incidental figure from another instant. A related role, subgroup or institution cannot replace the people the source names without an identity link in the moment or its bounded neighbors. This includes a narrator, speaker or listener who only frames the moment (reporting "I saw" or telling a story is not being there), and a cast member from an earlier or later step or event, including a later step of the moment's own text. A no-form cast member represented through effects must belong to this instant too; a section-wide look or a mere mention does not establish its manifestation here. Ordinary scenery, light, weather and effects that do not represent cast are not outside_instant. Use its cast id, or an empty id when it has no entry.
- not_one_instant: the fields give one character or prop two incompatible poses, places or support states (for example kneeling in one field and still walking up in another, or lying in one and sitting up in another), or present successive actions as happening together (for example steps joined by "then", or "does X and afterwards Y"). Ordinary simultaneous detail is fine.
- embodied_formless: a cast entry with hasForm false is given a body, face, hair, clothing, silhouette or figure, or is described as seated, sitting, enthroned or occupying a seat. This includes calling its effects seated or enthroned (for example "light seated above the throne"). Permitted effects such as light, fire or cloud placed at or around an unoccupied seat are fine. Naming a figure only to deny it is not a problem.
Before returning a verdict, make both checks across all seven scene fields:
1. Source support: examine every selected or described cast member, including a no-form member already in present. Selection supplies canon, not evidence that the subject belongs here. First identify who or what the source refers to, then compare that identity with the plan and selected IDs. Membership in a wider group, shared occupation, shared setting, similar appearance or a section-wide cast assignment does not establish that a narrower or different role is meant. For example, a passage about travelers does not by itself establish that they are the available guards. Report an unsupported substitution as outside_instant. A broader group entry may supply canon for its source-identified members without claiming the entire group is present; pronouns and continuing identities may resolve from bounded neighbors. Source-supported unnamed incidental roles remain allowed and do not require a cast entry. For a no-form effect, the current scene must establish the subject manifesting or acting within that scene; a command attributed to it, a curse, an oath, an invocation or a mention alone does not establish a visible manifestation.
